column1: # Defects a subplan knowingly shipped, and the checkpoint that owns resolving them.
# Read by test/guards/carrieddefects_test.go. A subplan that finds a defect it may not fix — because
# fixing it would change another subplan's frozen contract, or would exceed its own scope — records
# it here instead of in a commit body, where nothing enforces it. The guard makes the row load-
#   - Every UNRESOLVED row must name a live evidence test, so the defect cannot be silently fixed
#     and left recorded as broken, nor recorded and left unpinned.
#   - Every id must have a section in the detail document, so "what is this" always has an answer.
#   - No unresolved row may survive its RESOLVER's completion report. That is the gate: a wave
#     cannot be signed off with rows it was responsible for.
# `open` and `deferred:<checkpoint>` are both unresolved; only `fixed` and `wontfix` are not. A
# deferral names the LATER checkpoint that must dispose of the row, that checkpoint must have a
# plans/<checkpoint>-*.md document, and the row then blocks ITS report rather than its owner's.
#   id        stable identifier, <subplan>-D<n>, referenced from code comments and tests
#   opened_by the subplan that shipped the defect
#   owner     the checkpoint that must resolve or consciously re-defer it
#   evidence  test that pins the current behaviour, or "-" for rows with no runtime symptom
#   summary   one line, present tense, describing what is wrong
# Resolving a row means EITHER fixing the defect and setting status to `fixed`, OR setting it to
# `deferred:<later-checkpoint>` and adding the reason to the detail document. Both are conscious
# acts recorded in git history; neither can be reached by doing nothing.

column6: summary
JSON-escaped Windows temp paths are not canonicalized, so they fork the dedup space and carry user names into stored content
canonicalization is not idempotent when a deletion joins two fragments into a value neither half contained
one timestamp edge remains of the original three: a word byte after an ISO timestamp defeats the rule, and fixing it is legal only under fixed-point composition, so it travels with SP04-D2
devtool cover's landedSubplans must gain SP-02 and SP-03 at the wave-1 merge or their coverage floors stay off
canonicalization cost is now dominated by per-rule prefilter scans, so each new rule spends the hot-path budget linearly
BenchmarkRun_Bash100KB measured +-33% run to run on the reference host, which the 25% bench-compare threshold cannot distinguish from a regression

GCPolicy.Deadline binds the mark's hash harvest and the sweep, but tombstoneDeadRoots and the mark's index walks answer only to ctx, so GCReport.Duration can overshoot the deadline by the whole tombstone phase (100-260 ms measured at 650 dead roots)

a drain aborted by idle-budget expiry consumes the line it interrupted (offset advanced and seen-set committed before the binding completed), losing the event; the deliberate poison-line consume rule does not distinguish a dying drain from a refusing handler
the synthetic corpus raises only DemandFileContent, so tool_edit_distance, re_attempts and decision_preservation are measured over an input that cannot exercise them
file_set_jaccard is pinned at 1.0: the only repair re-reads the path key the demanding turn already touches, so the repaired set is the demanded set by construction
the Belady keep budget never binds on the corpus (oracle rewrite_span_tokens is 0 at every event), so fraction_of_opt grades against a trivial ceiling
belady.pMin iterates candidates where 5.2 defines it over all blocks; the deviation is recorded only in a code comment
decision_preservation measures post-compaction horizon agreement, which deterministic mode fixes at 1.0, not 11.2's pre-compaction decisions still recalled

the stock model deliberately carries no invoked-skills term: Qompack.md v1.5 retired 2.4 step 7 and its 25K figure as unverified host internals, the corpus raises no skill demand, and skills restore is covered by internal/rehydrate's skill index instead (the 4/3 hostPadTokens half is fixed and the stock model applies it)
canon.Decide has no consumer and 8.1's delta-vs-full storage write is implemented nowhere and owned by nobody

the PutBytes cold and warm budgets (3 ms / 400 us) are 5.2x and 14.1x over on Windows at V5 (15.74 / 5.65 ms, cold allocations up 28 % since the wave-3 baseline) and have never been measured on the reference platform

OnToolUse over a 256 KB tool result breaches budget B-C (l0_process, p99 < 50 ms): 53-115 ms on Qompack.md 8.1's own one-changed-line case and 262-655 ms when every chunk is novel, dominated by store.PutBytes's per-novel-chunk object-write path

Finalize measures 42.8-43.8 ms/op at 170-208 % processor performance but 64-73 ms/op at 128 % and at base clock on Windows against exit criterion 1570's 50 ms after perf(checkpoint) 72f3226 removed the paths.Norm share (264-284 ms before), and the reference platform has never been measured

negknow Open measures 258-273 ms CPU/op at 120 % processor performance but 586-633 ms at 55 % on Windows against its 300 ms budget, so the budget holds on this host only at turbo clocks, and the reference platform has never been measured

verify-on-read (16ecc77) adds an Lstat, an fstat and a content hash of the plaintext to every object read, so GetChunk measures 85-88 us/op (26 allocs) against the 60 us budget where the wave-3 baseline read 45 us (18 allocs), and Search_1000Roots, which reads every candidate chunk through the same path, 82 ms against 25 ms where the baseline read 45-52 ms; OpenSpan_4KB_of_4MB (19 -> 27 allocs) stays inside its 150 us at turbo but reads 316-333 us at base clock

putSideRecord content-addresses a delta side record over its deltas alone, so two roots whose canonicalization removed the same volatile token at the same offset share one record whose declared base is the first root: the second root's PutBytes reports FidelityExact and its RestoreOriginal fails with ErrDeltaCorrupt (latent: RestoreOriginal has no production caller, but the records persist)

the observer absorbs an at-least-once redelivery under a reused lease: captureSubagent recognizes the capture its own observation already published, through the capture sidecar, and derived ids are minted against the index rather than a process-local turn counter; a read's record and the supersede marks it authors land in one index write, so a replayed read appends no line and can no longer supersede records added after it. Residual: a process kill between a derived-id record and its sidecar link still re-captures (handed to SP08-D3), and the rule presumes an ObservationID is never reused for a different delivery (SP20-D4)

the leased Accept pays its three durability points (four fsyncs: WAL, lease, position temp file and directory) inside budget B-B's timed region, so l0_ingest cannot meet p99 < 2 ms on any host where an fsync costs more than about half a millisecond; bench-hotpath on this host measured p50 917.5 ms / p99 983.0 ms once the nonce fix made leases succeed, against 3.8 ms at V4 when every lease was refused

the shipped AckDeadlineMs of 8 ms is shorter than one leased Accept on this host (18-23 ms on a quiet AC window, 37-42 ms co-loaded), so the hook client spools a fallback copy of a delivery the daemon has already accepted - 25-26 of 196 hooks (13 %) in the two x09 runs on file, effectively every hook in bench-hotpath's burst - and every daemon start drains and skips work already done

an observe.prompt that reaches the daemon only by WAL or spool replay is never verbatim-captured: runIngested's prompt arm runs only the sentinel scan, the delivery is acknowledged and its spool copy deleted, so a prompt the daemon did not capture live (cold start, idle-exit respawn, connect failure, HotSpool, a crash before the capture landed) is lost, and a lost turn 0 makes the rehydrator inject a later prompt as the verbatim original

the delivery lease and acknowledgement journals cap at 65,536 entries and nothing retires either, so once a project has leased 65,536 deliveries every later delivery is refused a lease for good: it is still WAL-appended, ACKed and observed, but with no ObservationID, no capture sidecar and no committed frontier record, and a drain after a restart dispatches its copy a second time
